title: Embed bundle + subscription experiment for per-vector unit economics and rerank discounts
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Run a two-week experiment to evaluate per-vector unit pricing vs subscription bundles and explicit batch discounts for embeddings and reranking to determine optimal packaging for self-serve and enterprise customers.
background: We currently bill embeddings and reranking under simple per-unit rates with occasional ad-hoc discounts for large enterprise deals. Sales and finance report frequent objections from mid-market customers on unpredictable per-vector spend and from enterprise customers who prefer commitment-based discounts. This ticket captures an experiment and contract wording updates to validate the impact of subscription bundles (committed vectors per month) and explicit batch discounts (per-call discounts for bulk batch uploads) on adoption, churn, and ARR.
objective: Reduce friction for medium and enterprise customers by offering predictable cost options while preserving margin. Measure effect on conversion (trial->paid), average contract size, and net revenue retention over a pilot cohort.
success_metrics: +10% conversion from trial to paid for embedding-heavy trials within 30 days
+15% average contract value (ACV) for customers adopting bundles vs baseline
<5% increase in average RPS latency due to bundling infrastructure changes
unit economics: maintain >60% contribution margin after discounts
hypotheses: H1: Subscription bundles (committed vectors/mo) will increase willingness-to-pay and reduce invoice variability for mid-market buyers.
H2: Explicit batch discounts (e.g., 20% for bulk synchronous batch calls over 1M vectors) will reduce API misuse and increase throughput efficiency, lowering per-vector infra cost.
H3: Bundles plus a simple overage price outperform deeply tiered per-vector ladders for self-serve conversion.
experiment_design: Pilot cohorts: (A) baseline per-vector pricing (control), (B) tiered subscription bundles with overage pricing, (C) per-vector + explicit batch-discount tiers. Run for 8 weeks with 60-80 targeted customers: a mix of PLG signups showing embedding-heavy usage (self-serve) and 10 enterprise pilot customers identified by AE. Offer AEs a limited-time commit proposal (3 mo min). Track cost, usage profiles, churn signals, support tickets, and legal/contract negotiation time.
pricing_matrix: Bundle Bronze: $50/mo -> includes 100k vectors; overage $0.0007 per vector
Bundle Silver: $400/mo -> includes 1M vectors; overage $0.0005 per vector
Bundle Gold: $3,000/mo -> includes 10M vectors; overage $0.00035 per vector
Batch discount: 15% discount for synchronous batch calls >= 500k vectors per call; 25% discount for >= 1M vectors per call (applies to per-vector or overage price)
contract_qsa_asks: Update SOW sample language to explicitly enumerate bundled commitments and the mechanism for measuring 'vectors' (include edge cases: encoded token vs vectorized document count).
Add a billing appendix template for enterprise commitments showing monthly committed vectors, overage cadence, and credits/refunds policy.
Pre-authorize legal-approved discount caps for AEs (e.g., up to 30% on list across bundle + enterprise add-ons) and require finance sign-off for deeper discounts.

Clarify security/compliance statement: bundle pricing does not change data handling guarantees; ensure QSA includes billing changes in SOC2 scope as 'change to customer-facing controls' for next audit cycle.
stakeholder_feedback: Legal: prefer defined billing appendix templates and explicit measurement rules for vectors; flagged need to define dispute resolution for usage calculations.
Finance: wants 2-way sync with billing system; flagged recognition revenue implications for multi-month commitments.
Sales: supportive of commit-based bundles; requested playbook and AE-approved discount bands for quick negotiation.
Engineering: small runtime changes to enable batch discount flagging on ingest path; noted KV cache/throughput implications for large synchronous batches.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Customers misunderstand 'vector' definition leading to disputes. Mitigation: include canonical examples in SOW and a usage dashboard tile showing vector count by request.

Risk: Large batch discount could concentrate load causing latency spikes. Mitigation: enforce burst rate limits and route high-volume batch jobs to Dedicated pools where available; add a per-customer soft quota with alerts.
Risk: Revenue recognition complexity for multi-month prepay. Mitigation: Finance to prepare accounting treatment and prereconcile with legal before pilot.
